review.alternative: Training hesitation may arise from independent factors such as overtraining or physical burnout unrelated to AI usage.
review.would_change_mind: Longitudinal evidence showing that high-AI users retain or improve interoceptive accuracy over time.

claims.statement: AI-driven training recommendation reliance correlates with reduced self-regulation and increased decision hesitation in athletes.

support.explanation: This demonstrates a mechanism where externalized AI decision-making compromises internal regulation loops.
support.passage: A reduced sense of self-regulation was positively associated with training decision hesitation, which was further positively associated with reduced training self-efficacy.

actions.findings: AI-driven training recommendation reliance correlates with reduced self-regulation and increased decision hesitation in athletes. [source-d9addfec171d4b5d]
actions.limitations: Current evidence is limited to cross-sectional data, which cannot definitively establish the temporal or causal directionality of the observed associations.
actions.next_questions: Do longitudinal studies confirm whether chronic reliance on AI training recommendations permanently degrades an athlete's interoceptive awareness and self-regulation capacity?
actions.reason: Revising findings based on new evidence regarding systemic behaviors and scaling impacts on metric interpretation.
actions.summary: AI training recommendation dependence is strongly associated with a serial causal chain: body signal outsourcing leads to reduced self-regulation, which subsequently manifests as increased decision hesitation and reduced training self-efficacy.
actions.title: Revised AI Dependency and Reduced Autonomy in Athletes
